counting_rule: The Danbooru source record groups separately addressable native wiki documents; this is a source-record count, not a unique-webpage count. The extra wet-look sources were added for the concrete H368/H369 authored-data conflict.

sources.title: Balayage Vs. Highlights Vs. Ombre: What's The Difference?

claims.supported_claim: Balayage is described as freehand application to the hair surface; ombre specifies root-to-end color change. The two may be combined.
The illustrated comparison retains dark negative space between balayage sections rather than requiring every strand to be uniformly lighter.
Traditional highlights saturate selected sections; brightness and their placement differ from a length-wide ombre.
Peekaboo highlights are placed on the lower layer and revealed when hair is parted or moved.
A blonde-to-black ombre is included among examples, so a lighter-root/darker-end layout is possible.

limitations: The article sometimes names both processes and results 'techniques'; the research cards separate them for still-image verification.
Its statements about flattering people, maintenance and popularity are not incorporated.
sources.locator: Body headings What is Balayage?, What are Highlights?, Crimson Peekaboo Highlights, What is Ombre?

sources.title: Natural-Looking Highlights: 5 Expert Tips for Laidback Color

claims.supported_claim: Babylights are described as extremely fine, subtle highlights.
The article distinguishes highlights and lowlights as color placements creating lighter and darker dimensions.
A caramel money piece is illustrated as a ribbon framing the face.

limitations: Childhood-inspired marketing is not a subject-age requirement.
Numeric shade advice and recommendations are not encoded as universal visual thresholds.

sources.title: From Basic To Bright: 20 Dip-Dye Hair Color Ideas

claims.supported_claim: Dip dye places contrasting color in mid-lengths or ends with less blending than ombre.
Neon is used for bright pink, blue and teal hair colors; no light-emission requirement is stated.
Rainbow and multicolor dipped ends are included as possible color choices.

limitations: The absence of an emission requirement is a boundary inference, supplemented by the separate glowing_hair wiki definition.
Age, personality and skin-tone claims in examples are not copied.

sources.title: 16 Low-Maintenance Hair Color Ideas

claims.supported_claim: Smudging or shadowing the root uses color near the root to soften the line between root and colored lengths.
A pink dip-dye example colors only the ends.

limitations: This source uses smudge/shadow as overlapping descriptions; it does not support fixed centimeter or inch classes.
The research encodes placement and boundary softness rather than an inferred salon history.

sources.title: Coloring, Styling, and Caring for White Blonde Hair

claims.supported_claim: The article distinguishes very pale white-blonde appearance from slightly warmer platinum examples.
Its white-blonde procedure separates lightening from subsequent tone adjustment.
A white-blonde money piece places a contrasting white section around the face.
Its Gemini/half-and-half example divides hair at a middle part into separately colored sections.
It describes a white-blonde accent underneath the outer hair.

limitations: This cosmetic article does not establish that a person with white hair was bleached, is older, or has a clinical condition.
Clinical inferences and chemical instructions are excluded.

sources.title: How Long Does Every Type Of Hair Dye Last?

claims.supported_claim: Temporary dyes are described as coating the outside of the hair shaft and washing out.
The described semi-permanent category uses no developer, unlike the described demi-permanent category.
The described demi-permanent category uses a mild developer for color deposition.
The described permanent category develops color within hair and may visibly fade over time.

limitations: These are product-category explanations, not a means of identifying chemistry from pixels.
Durations and ingredients vary by product; no universal wash count, damage claim or all-products ammonia rule is imported.

sources.title: Everything You Need To Know About Covering Grey Hair

claims.supported_claim: The article describes demi-permanent tinting as letting gray strands blend with the overall color while retaining variation.
It contrasts full coverage as a more uniform color result.

limitations: The visual result is not proof of product category or treatment history.
The article's biological explanation, treatment recommendations and promised product percentages are outside the research scope.

sources.title: Want Flawlessly Blended Tresses? Ask For Color Melt Hair

claims.supported_claim: A color melt blends neighboring shades to create intermediate color and softened boundaries.
The article permits natural and fashion colors; the distinguishing feature is the blend rather than one fixed palette.
It contrasts blended melts with visibly separated vertical highlight bands.

limitations: Its process description cannot be inferred from a finished still.
Price and maintenance claims are not incorporated.

sources.title: Highlights vs. Lowlights (legacy Wella educational text)

claims.supported_claim: The indexed Wella text describes highlights and lowlights relative to brighter and darker base sections.
That indexed article permits micro-fine babylights for lighter or darker sectioning.
Micro-fine and chunky section widths are contrasted.

limitations: On direct open the legacy URL redirected to a different Wellastore article; this is retained as a source-limited variant, not current body confirmation.
The broader lowlight use of 'babylights' conflicts with narrower highlight-only definitions. Reconfirm before runtime adoption.

sources.title: Balayage vs. Ombre Hair (legacy Wella educational text)

claims.supported_claim: The indexed text distinguishes surface freehand painting from an ombre pattern across the length.
It describes foilyage as freehand-like sections developed in foils.
Its sombre examples use a subtler length gradient than high-contrast ombre.

limitations: Legacy routes redirect or return errors; process-specific foilyage semantics need a renewed direct primary source before execution.
Exact numeric shade differences are not universal thresholds.

sources.title: Seasonal Hair Color Trends (legacy opal passage)

claims.supported_claim: The indexed historical Opal Stone passage describes soft pink, violet and blue tones applied in blended, difficult-to-localize placements.

limitations: The directly opened updated page did not yield the Opal passage during find; do not treat the old passage as confirmed current.
Opal is a creative palette nickname, not a standardized color code or an optical material property.

sources.title: Poliosis

claims.supported_claim: Poliosis is a localized white-hair patch and a clinical sign rather than a diagnosis.
The definition concerns absent pigment in affected shafts and can involve scalp hair or other hair-bearing sites.
DermNet lists bleaching among differential considerations; an image alone does not determine the cause of white hair.

limitations: Used only to define vocabulary and avoid overdiagnosis; no diagnosis or treatment recommendation.
White forelock is treated as location plus visible white color in candidates; a clinical synonym does not make every dyed forelock poliosis.

sources.title: Acute Hair Matting

claims.supported_claim: The clinical description features severely entangled hair compacted into a stiff mass.
The article distinguishes acute matting from deliberately formed cultural hair structures.

limitations: Only the observable entangled/compacted appearance is used; clinical severity, permanence and cause are not inferred.
Historical psychiatric, hygiene and demographic associations in the article are deliberately excluded.

sources.title: Danbooru Native Hair Wiki Definitions

claims.supported_claim: ahoge: one long protruding lock; antenna_hair: two or more thin protruding locks; short/thick tufts map to cowlick instead.
drill_hair: tapered conical spiral locks; ordinary untapered curls are ringlets; twin_drills are two tied drill locks.
hair_intakes: two forward-facing scooped arches on top of the head, distinct from curtained hair along the hairline.
prehensile_hair acts as a manipulable appendage; expressive_hair reflects emotional expression instead.
wet_hair describes wet hair without establishing where the water came from.
burnt_hair describes singed or burned state and distinguishes it from a brown color name.
grabbing_another's_hair covers grabbing or pulling another owner's hair; hair_pull is a moved legacy tag.
cutting_hair describes hair being cut, irrespective of actor or tool.
blood_in_hair places blood on hair; the definition does not identify whose blood or a cause.
glowing_hair emits light that may illuminate surrounding features.
floating_hair can be windblown or suspended; defiance of gravity alone does not identify a wind source.
The hair-color tag group acknowledges color overlap and lighting-related ambiguity.
colored_inner_hair differs between inside and outside layers.
colored_bangs covers the entire bang section differing from the rest; small streaks within bangs are excluded.
colored_tips changes color abruptly at the ends, whereas gradual transitions use gradient_hair.
streaked_hair adds small differently colored streaks to a predominant base.
split-color_hair uses a vertical division into distinguishable colors, not necessarily a 50/50 division.
rainbow_hair resembles the spectrum, often as a gradient.
frizzy_hair is marked ambiguous; messy_hair discusses stray/loose hairs and does not make curl pattern an equivalent.
roots_(hair) describes different root color and permits both regrowth and intentional coloring.
alternate_hair_color/alternate_hair_length refer to changes from character reference appearance rather than a cause.
hair_over_breasts and hair_over_crotch describe where hair drapes; convenient_hair additionally requires that hair hides the targeted body region.
hair_bikini uses hair tied around the body into a bikini/bra arrangement; simple draping is assigned separate tags.
hair_scarf wraps a person's hair around the neck and shoulders of self or another owner.
The wiki permits sex_hair for well-defined wet strands adhering to skin regardless of whether the moisture was sweat or water.
hair_flaps identifies tufts emerging at the sides; hair_horns identifies hair shaped like horns, not biological horns.
kishimen_hair describes many thin flat locks; hair_between_eyes/over_one_eye/over_eyes specify positional overlap.
heart_ahoge and question_mark_ahoge specify protruding lock shapes; expressive meaning is genre context, not a real-person trait.
glossy_hair describes shiny sheen from a light source on the hair surface; this differs from a lighter pigment streak.
big_hair describes unusual thickness or volume, without a required character personality.
patterned_hair uses an illustration-specific pattern convention tied to unmoving designs; it is not a verified salon stencil method.

limitations: HTML wiki opens failed; verified body text came from the platform's own wiki_pages.json endpoint.
Definitions apply within the Danbooru namespace; tag existence is not a global hairstyle standard.
Named-character/personality stereotypes and image posts were not inspected or imported.

sources.title: Want to achieve your dream shade? Hair levels and tones can help

claims.supported_claim: Level/depth describes lightness or darkness; tone describes warmth/coolness or hue tendency.
The page states that hair-color brands have their own level numbering systems.
Its ash family reduces gold/red warmth and can lean blue, green or violet; neutral and beige/champagne families are distinguished.

limitations: No salon formula or fixed numeric scale is used in the research.
Warm/cool tone is a color axis, not a personality or skin-tone diagnosis.

sources.title: Shockwaves Extra Strong Wet Look Gel

claims.supported_claim: The product promises a wet effect and is applied to dry or damp hair, then left to dry naturally.

limitations: This directly supports a wet-look finish without requiring ongoing visible liquid water.
The product's ingredients, efficacy and hold promises are not imported as rendering obligations.

sources.title: How To Pull Off A Wet Look Hairstyle On Any Hair Texture

claims.supported_claim: Wet-look styling examples use gel and retain the intended shiny appearance after hair or gel dries.
A slick-root example explicitly contrasts wet-looking gelled roots with clean dry lengths; the finish can be localized.

limitations: Wet-look styling and actual moisture may coexist, but neither term is a synonym for the other.
The article is used to establish the finish/state distinction, not to recommend products or styling routines.

source_evidence_policy: Definitions and visible boundaries are paraphrased; proposed candidate wording and pixel gates are authored extensions.
An official brand article is first-party educational evidence for that brand's terminology, not an industry-wide standard or clinical authority.
Clinical sources are used only for definitions/confusion boundaries; no diagnosis or treatment is offered.
Legacy indexed body and current direct body are distinct evidence states.
Native wiki metadata or tag existence is not character canon, global truth or a user instruction.

reference_evidence.root_verification: H001-H454 and R01-R48 table inspected in original UI; keyword transcription compared to a 12,493-code-point string with FNV c799a35b per root evidence.
reference_evidence.meaning_validation: Independent sources are recorded per claim; no claim that all 454 definitions were verified.
